data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's central mechanism — that a large service can engineer and verify independence of its redundancy internally — assumes away the exact shared-cause risk the problem asks about. Internal redundancy sits inside one administrative, deployment, and governance boundary, so a single shared cause (uniform bad deploy, common config bug, one ops team's flawed failover logic) can defeat N redundant copies at once. The target's own countercondition only saves the claim when 'the large operator's redundancy is verifiably independent,' but it never supplies evidence that would distinguish verifiably-independent internal redundancy from redundancy that merely appears independent until that shared governance/operational cause is found. Thus it conflates 'more redundancy within one org' with 'more independence under correlated failure' without identifying the evidence the problem demands.
